newsitem.title: USA: Tropical Storm Josephine born in Gulf of Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Tropical Storm Josephine born in Gulf of Mexico.

text.p: Tropical Storm Josephine was born in the Gulf of Mexico on Sunday with 45 mph (72 kph) winds and a track that would take it ashore in Florida on Tuesday, the National Hurricane Center said.
A tropical storm watch, alerting residents to storm conditions within 36 hours, was issued for the Florida panhandle and the state's west coast from Apalachicola to Venice.
At 11 p.m. (0300 GMT), the center of Josephine was located at latitude 25.7 north, longitude 90.0 west, about 200 miles (320 km) south of New Orleans.

The storm was moving east-northeast at 13 mph (21 kph) and was expected to move ashore on Tuesday, though tropical storm- force winds were likely to be felt along the Florida coast on Monday, forecasters said.

National Hurricane Center forecaster Max Mayfield said the storm's threat was complicated by a high pressure system to the north of it that was helping create strong winds and heavy rain across much of the northern half of the Gulf of Mexico.
"This is a very complicated system. There is coastal flooding in southeast Louisiana ... due to the combination of the tropical storm and the strong high pressure," said Mayfield.
He said the two systems created the prospect of serious coastal flooding in vulnerable areas of the northeastern Gulf.
Josephine will probably strengthen slightly, but was not expected to reach hurricane strength before landfall, Mayfield said.
Tropical depressions become tropical storms and are given names when maximum winds reach 39 mph (62 kph) and gain hurricane status when winds hit 74 mph (119 kph).
